items.followUp: Name the three types of blood vessels and state which one connects arteries to veins.

rubric.why: The three vessels of the blood vascular system are identified.
rubric.description: Names the three types of blood vessels.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for all three names; award 1 mark for any two correct names.

modelAnswer: The blood vessels are arteries, veins and capillaries.

items.followUp: Define an ecosystem and distinguish it from a community.

rubric.why: A population consists of members of the same species living in a particular area.
rubric.description: Defines population.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the idea of the same species living in a particular area; award 1 mark if only one part is stated.

rubric.why: A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in an area.
rubric.description: Defines community.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for different populations/species in the same area; award 1 mark if only one part is stated.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in a particular area.
A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.
For example, all the frogs of one species in a pond form a population; the pond community includes its plants, animals and microorganisms.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and function of the centrosome in an animal cell.

rubric.why: Centrioles usually occur as a pair in animal cells.
rubric.description: States that centrioles occur in pairs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the pair.

rubric.why: The two centrioles are positioned at right angles to each other.
rubric.description: States their relative arrangement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the perpendicular arrangement.

rubric.why: The characteristic centriole structure is nine triplets of microtubules.
rubric.description: Describes the microtubule arrangement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for nine triplets of microtubules.

rubric.why: The centriole pair is located near the nucleus in the cell.
rubric.description: Gives the location of centrioles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating them near the nucleus.

rubric.why: Centrioles help organize spindle fibres during cell division.
rubric.description: States their role in cell division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for their role in spindle formation during cell division.

modelAnswer: Centrioles are small cylindrical structures found in animal cells, usually near the nucleus.
They occur as a pair, with the two centrioles arranged at right angles to each other.
Each centriole consists of nine triplets of microtubules arranged in a cylinder.
Centrioles help organize spindle fibres during cell division.
They are also involved in the formation of cilia and flagella.

items.followUp: Explain how pH and enzyme concentration affect enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Low temperature reduces molecular movement and slows enzyme action.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of low temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that low temperature slows enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Enzyme activity is highest at its optimum temperature.
rubric.description: Identifies the optimum temperature effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that activity rises to a maximum at the optimum.

rubric.why: Excessive heat changes an enzyme's shape, including its active site, and denatures it.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of excessive temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for denaturation or change of the active site at high temperature.

rubric.why: Increasing substrate concentration raises the rate until enzyme active sites are occupied and the rate levels off.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of substrate concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the increase in rate and its levelling off at saturation.

modelAnswer: At low temperatures, enzyme activity is slow because molecules move more slowly.
As temperature rises, enzyme activity increases until it reaches a maximum at the enzyme's optimum temperature.
Above the optimum temperature, the enzyme is denatured; its active site changes shape and its activity falls.
Increasing substrate concentration increases the reaction rate while more substrate can bind to enzyme active sites.
The rate eventually levels off when all active sites are occupied.

items.followUp: Describe the role of ATP and NADPH in the Calvin cycle.

rubric.why: The dark reactions are associated with the work of Melvin Calvin.
rubric.description: Names the discoverer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Melvin Calvin.

rubric.why: The reactions take place in the stroma of chloroplasts.
rubric.description: States the site of the reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the chloroplast stroma.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide is fixed by combining with RuBP.
rubric.description: States the carbon-fixation step.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for carbon dioxide combining with RuBP.

rubric.why: ATP and NADPH are used to reduce the carbon-fixation products to PGAL.
rubric.description: Describes the reduction step and its energy sources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the use of ATP and NADPH in forming PGAL.

rubric.why: Some PGAL is used to make sugars, while the remainder regenerates RuBP.
rubric.description: States the products and regeneration step.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for sugar formation and/or regeneration of RuBP.

modelAnswer: The dark reactions were worked out by Melvin Calvin and are also called the Calvin cycle.
They occur in the stroma of chloroplasts and do not use light directly; they use ATP and NADPH made during the light reactions.
Carbon dioxide combines with RuBP (ribulose bisphosphate) and is fixed into an intermediate that forms PGA.
ATP and NADPH are used to reduce PGA to PGAL.
Some PGAL is used to make sugars, while the rest regenerates RuBP so the cycle can continue.

items.followUp: Name the four most abundant elements in living organisms.

rubric.why: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen are four of the six main bioelements.
rubric.description: Names the first four main bioelements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all four elements.

rubric.why: Phosphorus and sulfur complete the six main bioelements.
rubric.description: Names the remaining two main bioelements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both phosphorus and sulfur.

modelAnswer: The six main bioelements are carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur.

items.followUp: What is colonial organization? Give one example.

rubric.why: Colonial organization involves similar organisms or cells living together as a colony.
rubric.description: Defines colonial organization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that similar organisms/cells live together in a colony.

rubric.why: Volvox is a standard example; cells in a colony may retain some ability to function independently.
rubric.description: Gives an example or relevant feature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as Volvox, or for noting that cells retain some independence.

modelAnswer: In colonial organization, similar cells or organisms live together in a group called a colony.
The cells cooperate but may retain some ability to carry out their own functions; Volvox is an example.

items.followUp: How did Ronald Ross provide evidence that mosquitoes transmit malaria?

rubric.why: King observed an association between the occurrence of malaria and the presence of mosquitoes.
rubric.description: States the geographical association.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking malaria occurrence with the presence or distribution of mosquitoes.

rubric.why: His observations also linked malaria with mosquito abundance, mosquito bites or protection from mosquitoes.
rubric.description: States another relevant observation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant observation such as increased malaria in the rainy season, protection by mosquito nets, or the link with mosquito bites.

modelAnswer: A. F. A. King observed that malaria was common in places where mosquitoes were abundant and was uncommon where mosquitoes were absent.
He also noted that malaria increased in the rainy season, when mosquitoes were plentiful, and that mosquito nets could help protect people from the disease.
